The '''2017 [[Eliteserien]]''' was the 73rd completed season of top-tier [[Association football|football]] in [[Norway]]. The season began on 1 April 2017 and ended on 26 November 2017, not including play-off matches. This was first season of Eliteserien as rebranding from Tippeligaen.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.fotball.no/turneringer/eliteserien/2016/spilleplan-2017 | title=Slik spilles Eliteserien 2017 | publisher=www.fotball.no | date=19 December 2016 | access-date=19 December 2016}}</ref> [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] were the defending champions, while [[Kristiansund BK|Kristiansund]] and [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] entered as the promoted teams from the [[2016 1. divisjon]].

The 2017 season saw the name of the league change from '''Tippeligaen''' (named after sponsor [[Norsk Tipping]]) to '''Eliteserien''', a non-sponsor affiliated name controlled by the [[Football Association of Norway]]. [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] won their third consecutive title and 25th top-flight title overall, with two games to spare. Rosenborg conceded only 20 goals during the season, a league record.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fotballen.eu/Emner/Tippeligaen_statistikk.html |title=Statistikk for den norske Eliteserien |language=no |access-date=26 June 2018 |archive-date=1 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301105139/https://www.fotballen.eu/Emner/Tippeligaen_statistikk.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Overview==
===Rebranding===
On 28 August 2016, the Football Association of Norway (NFF) and [[Norsk Toppfotball]]  announced a rebrand; beginning with the 2017 season, the competition was known simply as Eliteserien, without any sponsor's name attached. As part of the rebranding, a new logo was introduced.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fotball.no/tema/nff-nyheter/2016/eliteserien---lidenskap-og-fellesskap/ |title=Tippeligaen endrer navn til Eliteserien i 2017 |trans-title=Tippeligaen changes name to Eliteserien in 2017 |publisher=[[Football Association of Norway|NFF]] |date=28 August 2016 |access-date=10 December 2018 }}</ref>

===Summary===
[[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] won their third consecutive title and 25th top-flight title overall. Rosenborg were the defending champions, while [[Kristiansund BK|Kristiansund]] and [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] entered as the promoted teams from the [[2016 1. divisjon]].

Rosenborg won the league with two games to spare. [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]] and [[Viking FK|Viking]] were relegated directly. Fourteenth-finishers [[Sogndal Fotball|Sogndal]] were relegated after losing the [[2017 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs|play-off]] final to [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]].

==Teams==
Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top fourteen teams from the previous season, and two teams promoted from the [[2016 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]]. The promoted teams were [[Kristiansund BK|Kristiansund]] (first season in the top-flight) and [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]], (returning to the top flight after a season's absence). They replaced [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] and [[IK Start|Start]] ending their top flight spells of three and four years respectively.

==Relegation play-offs==
{{Main|2017 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs}}
The 14th-placed team, Sogndal took part in a two-legged play-off against [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]], the winners of the [[2017 1. divisjon#Promotion play-offs|1. divisjon promotion play-offs]], to decide who would play in the [[2018 Eliteserien]].
